description: The 'unit (macos-latest)' leg of .github/workflows/test-unit.yml is the slowest job in the pipeline (median 7.0 min, longest 9.5 min, against 3.2 min for 'unit (ubuntu-latest)' on the same heads) and runs on every pull request head. A relevance gate built as 'run unless every changed file is on a platform-neutral list' was replayed over the 74 merged pull requests #241 to #314 and would have skipped the macOS leg on none of them, because every flow pull request changes code. The gate must instead run the macOS leg only when a change touches something that can behave differently on macOS. A ported starting point exists on branch 'I-1795647400-macos-unit-only-when-relevant/P-1795666532-CLA-CO5.5/E-1795666668-CLA-CO5.5/_' (pull request #315, not merged): .github/actions/macos-relevance-gate/action.yml, scripts/macos_relevance.py, the 'ci-macos' label in scripts/ci_bookkeeping_gate.py, and tests test_macos_relevance.py and test_macos_relevance_wiring.py; reuse it where it fits.
goal: On pull requests, run the macOS unit leg only when at least one changed file matches a stated list of platform-sensitive paths or contents; otherwise skip the rest of the leg's steps so the job still completes with success under the check name 'unit (macos-latest)' (never skipped at job level). Platform-sensitive: dependency manifests and the lock file (pyproject.toml, uv.lock), every file under .github/ (workflows, actions), the gate script and its tests, shell scripts, Dockerfiles, and any Python source file whose content (new or old version) uses subprocess, os.path or pathlib filesystem operations beyond pure path joining, os.environ HOME handling, signal, sys.platform, platform., fcntl, termios, pty, resource, keychain or launcher code (state the exact content patterns, and the module paths treated as sensitive regardless of content). Tests count by the same rule as source. Deleted or renamed files are judged by their old path and old content. The leg always runs on push to main and when the 'ci-macos' label is present, and it runs when the changed-file list is empty or cannot be read. A skipped leg records no timing sample and does not fail the CI Timing Gate. Document the rule and its accepted risk (a macOS-only break in a file judged neutral is caught by the push-to-main run after merge) next to the bookkeeping gate in .github/workflows/README.md. Module line budgets (holon-config/hygiene/module_budgets.json) are frozen: never change that file; split a module that would exceed its limit.
rationale: The macOS leg sets the pipeline's wall-clock time and every CI wait in the flow; skipping it on pull requests that touch no platform-sensitive code takes about 3 minutes off most pull request heads, which a neutral-list gate cannot do.
acceptance_criteria: The execution notes replay the rule over the merged pull requests #241 to the newest merge and list, per pull request, whether the macOS leg would have run and the sensitive file that triggered it; the share of skipped pull requests is stated.

Unit tests cover: neutral-only Python change (skip), a change adding a subprocess or sys.platform use to a previously neutral file (run), a change removing such a use (run, judged on old content), pyproject.toml or uv.lock change (run), any .github/ change (run), shell script or Dockerfile change (run), the 'ci-macos' label (run), push to main (run), empty or unreadable changed-file list (run), deleted and renamed sensitive files (run).

On a skipping pull request, 'unit (macos-latest)' completes with success in under 1 minute and its log lists every judged path with its verdict; the check name is reported on every pull request head and the job has no job-level condition.
A skipped macOS leg records no timing sample and does not fail the CI Timing Gate; the ubuntu unit leg, the bookkeeping gate and the Workspace survival job are unchanged.
The execution notes give the macOS leg's measured time on this pull request's own CI run (it changes .github/, so the leg runs).
All tests pass via 'uv run pytest', and 'uv run task lint' and 'uv run task lint-docs' pass.
